input.rationale: Section 12 contains a broad Client indemnity (breach of Agreement, System/Credit Repository defaults, Web Site/Client Content, product liability) but TrueLink's indemnity is limited to its own breach of this Agreement or failure to perform; there is no third-party IP infringement indemnity anywhere in the Agreement (no infringement or IP indemnity language in Sections 1-11, and Section 2(d) merely reserves TrueLink's ownership). Under the detection guidance, a Vendor indemnity that excludes IP infringement fails the fallback, so this is a deviation. We target the preferred position: an inserted TrueLink defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement claims relating to the Interface, Hosting Services and Support Services, TrueLink's breach of law, TrueLink-caused unauthorized access to Client data, and its gross negligence or willful misconduct, with notice, control-of-defence and cooperation mechanics, and a narrowing of Client's indemnity to Client Content and Client's violation of law. We selected preferred rather than fallback because the fallback's 3x-annual-fees super-cap would introduce a new cap on an indemnity that is presently uncapped, weakening our position.

mappings.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

proposal.summary: Add TrueLink IP/misconduct indemnity with defence procedure; narrow Client's indemnity to Client Content and Client's breach of law
proposal.comment: [Playbook] TrueLink's indemnity covers only its own breach of this Agreement and omits third-party IP infringement, so we added a defence and indemnity for infringement claims relating to the Interface and services, TrueLink's breach of law, TrueLink-caused data breaches and its gross negligence or willful misconduct, together with the usual notice, control and cooperation mechanics. We also narrowed our indemnity to Client Content and Client's violation of law, consistent with our playbook position.

ops.text: c. TrueLink shall defend, indemnify and hold Client and its affiliates harmless from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (i) an allegation that the Interface, the Hosting Services or the Support Services infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right, (ii) TrueLink's breach of applicable law, (iii) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Client Content or other Client data caused by TrueLink, or (iv) TrueLink's gross negligence or willful misconduct. The indemnified party shall give the indemnifying party prompt written notice of any claim under this Section 12, the indemnifying party shall have control of the defense and settlement of such claim, and the indemnified party shall provide reasonable cooperation in the defense.

ops.oldText: (i) any claim arising out of any breach by Client of this Agreement, (ii) any claim or demand resulting from any act or omission by Client or any customer of Client granted access to the Interface by Client which constitutes a breach of or default by TrueLink under any System Agreement or Credit Repository Agreement, which breach or default has either not been cured or cannot be cured within the applicable cure period and the consequences of which is that TrueLink will lose material rights it has pursuant to said Agreements or a violation of any state or federal law, rule or regulation (iii) any claim arising out of or relating to the Web Site or Client Content (including, but not limited to, any claim resulting from any content posted to the Web Site by Client or Client's employees, agent or any customer of Client granted access to the Interface by Client), without regard to any knowledge limitation or qualification that may be contained in this Agreement, and (iv) injury or damage to person or property caused by a product, service, or information, whether or not defective, that is sold, distributed or transmitted from the Web Site.
